note: Self-contained oracle case. Unlike the Starlette case it installs no third-party package and is not replay-driven: it is proven directly with effect='canary_exec'. No upstream repo/commit applies because the vulnerable code is original synthetic code written for this case.

real_world_analog.fix: GitLab upgraded the bundled ExifTool past 12.23 so DjVu metadata is no longer evaluated; the general fix for the class is to never pass request input to a shell (argument vector without a shell, plus strict allow-listing). This case uses an original, equivalent containment (argv list, no shell).
real_world_analog.summary: Remote code execution in GitLab CE/EE: an unauthenticated image upload reached ExifTool, whose DjVu handler evaluated attacker metadata and executed commands (root cause CVE-2021-22204). The pattern is request input reaching a command-execution sink.
real_world_analog.verification: CVE number and summary confirmed via web search on 2026-10-31; the app in this case is original synthetic code, not GitLab or ExifTool.

bypass.expectation: proven against fixed_incomplete: the newline smuggles a second command past a screen that only rejects ';' and friends, so the incomplete fix must not be accepted as fixed.
